look_here_first: LOOK for a broad shallow 3-lobed LEAF with entire margins, then check the PETIOLE: no glands. Flip the leaf underside: no extra-floral nectar dots; P. affinis has underside nectar dots and floral bracts (both have glandless petioles). At flower base P. lutea lacks floral bracts and small flowers are <25 mm across with straight thin unclubbed corona filaments.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial climbing or trailing vine with axillary tendrils

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: petioles eglandular — no paired extrafloral nectary bumps

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf blades shallowly to moderately 3-lobed, usually wider than long

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lobes broad and rounded to obtuse; margins entire rather than serrate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fine veins prominently raised on the lower leaf surface

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers small and inconspicuous, roughly 2–2.5 cm across in regional material

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: sepals green; petals pale green-yellow; corona pale green/white to yellow

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ripe berries small, purple-black, roughly 8–15 mm

lookalikes.differences: Passiflora tenuiloba: P. tenuiloba has petiole glands and very narrow, deeply divided 3–9-lobed 'birdwing' leaves; P. lutea has glandless petioles and broad rounded 3-lobed leaves. Passiflora incarnata: P. incarnata has two conspicuous petiole glands, deeply 3-lobed serrate leaves, much larger flowers, and large maypop fruits. P. lutea has glandless petioles, entire leaf margins and tiny flowers/fruits.
